title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages. K ⊂ L are fields of characteristic 0, with L of finite type over K and K of finite type over Q. E_L denotes the Galois extension 1 → Gal(L̄/LK̄) → Gal(L̄/L) → Gal(K̄/K) → 1, viewed as an extension of E_K = Gal(K̄/K). A 'section of E_L over E_K' is a splitting of this sequence. A 'germ of section' is a splitting over some open subgroup of Gal(K).

General principle (previous pages). Sections can be built from the 'points of dimension 0 of the Riemann (Zariski–Riemann) variety' of L/K. These are the valuation rings V of L containing K whose residue field is algebraic (here finite) over K.
- For such a V one has a decomposition group N_V and an inertia group I_V.
- N_V/I_V is the Galois group of the residue field, which maps isomorphically onto an open subgroup of Gal(K).
- In characteristic 0, N_V → N_V/I_V splits. Hence one gets germs of sections of E_L over E_K, each normalizing I_V.

This page. Let L_1 ⊂ L be a subextension of transcendence degree 1 over K (a function field of a curve).
- Composing with the restriction map E_L → E_{L_1} turns each (germ of) section of E_L into a (germ of) section of E_{L_1} over E_K.
- So the 'Riemann variety' construction for L gives a second way to produce sections for the curve L_1.
- The question is whether this yields sections of E_{L_1} beyond those already attached to the places of L_1/K.

Answer: no. Put V_1 = V ∩ L_1. This is a valuation ring of L_1. Its residue field lies inside that of V, so it is finite over K. Hence V_1 ≠ L_1, since otherwise the residue field would be L_1, which is transcendental over K. So V_1 is a place of the curve.

The next page completes the argument by functoriality. E_L → E_{L_1} sends N_V into N_{V_1} and I_V into I_{V_1}. So the induced germ of section normalizes I_{V_1}, and on the open part E_K^0 it centralizes I_{V_1}.

The next page then states the higher-dimensional birational section conjecture: every (germ of) section of E_L over E_K normalizes the inertia group I_V of a valuation V of L/K with algebraic residue field, V being unique.

Left-margin note: one can reduce here to K = Q ('K → Q') in the case where K is of finite type over Q.

Purpose: consistency check showing that the valuation-theoretic source of sections in higher dimension is compatible with, and reduces to, the curve case under restriction to transcendence-degree-1 subfields.
errors: No mathematical error. The argument that V_1 is nontrivial is only implicit on this page and is made explicit on the next page.
'Sous-extension L_1 de K' should read 'of L/K' (a subextension of L over K) – a slip of the pen or of the transcription.
The phrase 'Mais il en est bien ainsi' must logically mean that no new sections arise this way (the image sections are the place-type ones). The wording is slightly ambiguous.

ideas.what: Germs of Galois sections attached to zero-dimensional points (valuations with residue field algebraic over K) of the Zariski–Riemann space of L/K, via decomposition/inertia groups
ideas.modern_name: Birational (valuative) section conjecture; sections arising from decomposition groups of valuations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983); later Koenigsmann, Pop, Esnault–Wittenberg for birational variants
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983) states the section conjecture including birational variants; the Longue Marche notes themselves are unpublished

ideas.what: Compatibility of valuation-type sections with restriction to transcendence-degree-1 subfields: V∩L_1 is a place of the curve, and N_V→N_{V_1}, I_V→I_{V_1}
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of decomposition and inertia groups under field restriction

missed.claim: This is an early formulation (around 1981) of the higher-dimensional birational section conjecture in terms of zero-dimensional points of the Zariski–Riemann space. It comes with the observation that, via subcurves L_1, sections of valuation type restrict to place-type sections. This anticipates later reduction-to-curves strategies, but the content itself is known.
missed.quote: un principe général pour construction des germes de sections de E_L sur E_K — à l'aide des pts de dim 0 de la "variété de Riemann" de L sur K
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents the historical origin of the birational section conjecture for higher-dimensional function fields; mathematically no new result.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine functoriality check within the section-conjecture program. The birational and higher-dimensional formulation is of some historical interest, but the conjecture is well known and attributed to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: 'Compte tenu[?], pour une sous-extension' likely reads 'Composant, pour une sous-extension'.
The dash after E_{L_1} is probably 'avec' ('Composant ... avec l'homom. E_L → E_{L_1}').
Margin probably: 'on peut ici K → Q, au cas où K de type fini sur Q bien sûr!' (reduction to base Q).
